Reinforcement learning, one idea at a ti.intro: The main ideas of reinforcement learning, in the order that each one needs the one before. Each article asks one question and answers it with robots that learn, fail and get fixed in Breaking Bellman, a small browser game.

parts.title: Q-learning: one table for the value and the policy
parts.question: How can one table of numbers tell a robot both how good a situation is and what to do in it?

parts.title: Bootstrapping: learning from your own guess
parts.question: Why does a learner use its own guess as a target, and what does that buy?

parts.title: Function approximation: learning about situations you never saw
parts.question: What does a robot gain, and what can it lose, when one formula replaces the table?

parts.title: On-policy and off-policy: whose behavior does the target describe?
parts.question: Should a learner's target describe the behavior that collects the data, or a better behavior?

parts.title: The deadly triad: when three good ideas run away together
parts.question: Why can bootstrapping, function approximation and off-policy learning make values run away together, when two of the three can often avoid it?
